text:
AcmeOps: Hey team — customers in APAC are getting 429s right now. Started ~2026-03-17T10:12:00Z. We see hundreds/sec for a few minutes. Example response: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests\nRetry-After: 6\nX-Request-ID: acme-req-9f2a\n{\"error\":\"rate limit exceeded\"}`

Mia (support): Thanks — can you paste a sample x-request-id and whether this is the hosted API or Dedicated? Also which model/route and roughly tokens per request?

AcmeOps: It's hosted, route `POST /v1/generate`, model `redwood-3-large`, tokens ~120 per call. Sample x-request-id: `acme-req-9f2a`. Region eu-west has most traffic. We do see `X-Rate-Limit-Remaining: 0` in a bunch of responses.

Jordan (SRE): Noted. Can you confirm whether clients are bursting (many short requests) or steady high throughput? Also any recent deploys?

AcmeOps: Turned out to be a cronjob we rolled out yesterday that fires 150 workers at once to refresh embeddings+summaries. They all call the generation endpoint in parallel, so it's a short spike lasting ~30–90s every hour. No deploys from our side.

deploy-bot: recent rate-limiter config change deployed 02:15 UTC — default per-customer RPM cap lowered from 600 -> 450 in eu-west (rollout 80%).

Liam (eng-runtime): That config change combined with a 150-worker spike will hit the RPM bucket hard. RPM vs TPM: RPM is per-minute request token bucket; TPM is token-per-minute. Because each request is small tokens (~120), this looks like RPM exhaustion.

Mia (support): Quick mitigations: 1) Can you throttle workers to stagger them (e.g., jitter + spread over minute). 2) Use client-side batching/aggregation for small requests. 3) Short-term we can open a temporary soft quota bump while customers fix their cron. Would you like that?

AcmeOps: We'd appreciate a temporary bump for the next 2 hours while we patch the cron job. Can you also point us to recommended backoff headers we should honor? Some clients ignore Retry-After.

Jordan (SRE): We'll do the bump. Recommended behavior: honor `Retry-After` seconds header, exponential backoff with jitter, cap retries to 3 for idempotent calls. Example: `sleep = min(60, base * 2^attempt) + random(0, base)` where base=1s. Also add client-side concurrency limit (e.g., max in-flight 10).

Liam (eng-runtime): Adding a sample curl and expected header parsing to honor Retry-After: 
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \\\
  -d '{"model":"redwood-3-large","input":"..."}'
```
Look for `Retry-After` and back off before retrying. If you see `X-Rate-Limit-Reset` use that to schedule next attempt.

Rebecca (CS): I'll coordinate the quota bump with the customer and send a confirmation. Also I'll ask them to share the patched cron by EOD so we can close the ticket.

Mia (support): Action items: 1) SRE (Jordan) will apply a 1-hour soft RPM increase for org `acme-corp` in eu-west. 2) Eng (Liam) will add a quick check to logs for `acme-req-9f2a` pattern and collect histogram of per-minute requests from that org over last 24h. 3) AcmeOps will roll out cron patch to add jitter and reduce concurrency. 4) CS (Rebecca) will confirm and message customer.

Jordan (SRE): Applying soft bump now — set RPM from 450 -> 1200 for acme-corp for 60 minutes. I'll post when done.

Jordan (SRE): Done — soft bump applied at 2026-03-17T10:28:04Z. Monitor for 10m and we can extend if needed.

AcmeOps: Thanks — seeing errors drop immediately. We'll push a deferred rollout with jitter within the hour. Appreciate the quick help :heart:

Mia (support): Closing loop — I'll keep this thread updated if anything else pops up. If you want a permanent quota change we'll need product approval and usage commit.

AcmeOps: Understood. One follow-up: is there a recommended server-side pattern we could use to avoid needing huge RPMs in the future?

Liam (eng-runtime): Recommended: 1) use batch endpoints for bulk work 2) maintain a queue worker that paces requests 3) cache common prefixes/results (KV cache) and reuse embeddings when possible. We can share a checklist/snippet for converting their cron to a queued job — cc @Rebecca to coordinate.
